sentences.text: Butyricimonas species are Gram-negative, anaerobic bacteria that form part of the human gut microbiota.
The genus was proposed for obligately anaerobic, non-motile Gram-negative rods isolated from rat faeces that produced significant levels of butyric and isobutyric acids from glucose.
A review of reported human Butyricimonas infections compiled 14 publications describing 14 patients, with a history of malignancy the most frequently reported predisposing factor.
That review reported that such infections are extremely rare in clinical practice and occur more often in immunocompromised individuals or patients with significant underlying health conditions.
In mice fed a high-fat diet, gavage with Butyricimonas virosa was reported to suppress progression of steatotic liver disease and to enhance production of thiamine monophosphate.
